definitions.explanation: Strikingly unusual or odd, enough to attract attention or cause discomfort.

examples.japanese: {奇異|きい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{感|かん}じた→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。

examples.english: He didn't seem to notice the people around him looking at him strangely.

notes:
A somewhat formal word for strangeness that implies something is unusual enough to draw attention. Often used to describe how others perceive unusual behavior.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {奇異|きい}な⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ — to look at someone strangely
- {奇異|きい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧ — strange looks, looks of bewilderment
- {奇異|きい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧ — to find something strange
- {奇異|きい}な⟦{光景|こうけい}→光景：02799_koukei⟧ — a bizarre sight
- {奇異|きい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{映|うつ}る→映る：12964_utsuru⟧ — to appear strange

USAGE:
The phrase {奇異|きい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ / {奇異|きい}な⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ is the most common usage — it means to stare at someone as if they are bizarre. This expression implies social judgment and discomfort.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{奇妙|きみょう}→奇妙：01630_kimyou⟧ — strange, curious (lighter, can be intriguing)
- ⟦{不思議|ふしぎ}→不思議：02358_fushigi⟧ — mysterious, puzzling (more neutral, can be positive)
- ⟦{異様|いよう}→異様：13550_iyou⟧ — bizarre, abnormal (stronger, more alarming)
